subject: Any way to 'sweep' angle with scale_area?

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Any way to 'sweep' angle with scale_area?
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to use scale_area with the two point geoms, a large white
point of fixed size and a black point whose area 'fills' the white
point (by virtue of being layered on top). I notice that the results,
while correct, aren't perceptually very helpful because of the way
area grows quadratically as radius increases.

What would be very helpful is if the shape of the black points
resembled a pie whose area was swept out by increasing angles.
Readers of the charts would be much more familiar with, say, a pie
chart swept 75% than a circle with 75% of its area filled in from the
center out.

Any ideas on how something like this could be done?

Thanks,
Mauricio

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Any way to 'sweep' angle with scale_area?
parts:
The only way you could currently do this would be to draw the circles
yourself using basic trigonometry + geom_polygon. This isn't actually
too hard - if you supplied a reproducible example, I could get you
started.

Hadley

If you get frustrated with trig and geom_polygon, one way to accomplish the visualization you are after is to position the lowest point of the varying black circle at the lowest point of the fixed white circle. 

Good luck,

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Re: Any way to 'sweep' angle with scale_area?
parts:
Hadley ... thanks so much for your offer to help. Here is a
reproducible example.

#The following is tab-delimited data.

Question Score RR
1 0.71 0.44
2 0.89 0.75
3 1 0.38
4 0.86 0.44
5 0.78 0.56

#After saving the data to some file ...
dframe <- file.choose()
p <- ggplot(dframe, aes(x=Question, y=Score))
p <- p + geom_point(aes(size=1), shape=1, legend=TRUE) +
geom_point(aes(size=RR))
p + scale_area(limits=c(0,1), breaks=c(.2, .4, .6, .8, 1), to=c(0,5))

#Something else to note: use of "legend=TRUE" is not forcing the
background circle to appear in the legend.

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Re: Any way to 'sweep' angle with scale_area?
parts: Please note the comment "Use of 'legend=TRUE' is not forcing the
background circle to appear in the legend."

Addressing this would be a very simple solution that would avoid the
trigonometry. Showing readers what a filled-in circle looks like at
different rates of filling would go a long way toward overcoming their
lack of familiarity with 'from the center out' shading.

Any help would be most welcome.

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Re: Any way to 'sweep' angle with scale_area?
parts:
I've modified my code for making it easier to reproduce. The priority
would be on how to make the scale legend combine both point geoms.
This would be a 'good enough' alternative to 'swept out' circles.

Category <- as.factor(1:5)
Score <- runif(5)
Density <- runif(5)
dframe <- data.frame(Category, Score, Density)
p <- ggplot(dframe, aes(x=Category, y=Score))

Thanks so much for the help,
Mauricio
